learningObjective: Diagnose why an autotuner-chosen tile size regressed on a new shape and identify the trade-off that triggered it.

canonicalClaims.claim: A tile size tuned on a large shape can under-utilize a many-SM GPU on a smaller shape because the resulting grid contains too few blocks to fill all SMs; the fix is smaller tiles, split-K, or persistent kernels.
conditions: The GPU has substantially more SMs than the grid block count at the smaller shape.
Split-K or persistent-kernel strategies are not already enabled.
nonImplications: Does not imply the smaller tile is universally superior — on the original large shape the larger tile was optimal.
Does not imply retuning is the only remedy; kernel-side split-K is an alternative.

misconceptions.claim: A tuned tile size generalizes across all shapes because it captures the hardware's intrinsic best block dimension.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The best tile size interacts with the total grid count, which is shape-dependent; no single tile is optimal for all shapes.

misconceptions.claim: Tensor Cores require GEMM dimensions to be exact multiples of the tile block dimension (e.g., 128).
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tensor Cores require multiples of the MMA fragment (e.g., 16); larger tile blocks handle any dimension divisible by the fragment, with masked tail blocks for remainders.

misconceptions.claim: Low Tensor-Core utilization on small grids indicates that Nsight Compute is misreporting; the kernel is actually running near peak.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TC utilization is measured across active cycles; if many SMs are idle, aggregate TC utilization is genuinely low.

misconceptions.claim: Reducing tile size always improves performance on small shapes because it always increases grid count.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Below some threshold, arithmetic intensity per tile falls below the peak-Tensor-Core requirement and per-tile efficiency drops.

implementationFacts: A100 has 108 SMs; H100 has 132 (or 144 in some variants).
Split-K adds an extra reduction along K to increase grid block count while keeping large per-tile K-reuse.
Persistent kernels re-use blocks to iterate over more work per launch.
performanceScenarios: M=N=K=1024 with 128×128 tile = 64 blocks; on A100 fills ~59% of SMs at best.
Same shape with 64×64 tile = 256 blocks, oversubscribing 108 SMs by 2.4×.
